articles.title: Lightweight C++ CSPRNG Implementation for Custom Schnorr Zero-Knowledge Proofs Without Heavy Libraries
articles.excerpt: Evaluating the cryptographic soundness of a custom Schnorr zero-knowledge proof implementation requires examining how data flows from raw entropy generation through commitment binding, Fiat-Shamir cha…
articles.body: Protocol Architecture Audit: Anatomy of a Custom Schnorr ZKP Evaluating the cryptographic soundness of a custom Schnorr zero-knowledge proof implementation requires examining how data flows from raw entropy generation through commitment binding, Fiat-Shamir challenge derivation, and final scalar validation. In educational repositories such as dev-dawud/ZeroKnowledgeProof , the core vulnerability rarely stems from syntax errors, but rather from the silent breakdown of mathematical assumptions when low-level primitives are poorly constructed. The foundation of any Schnorr protocol rests on the ephemeral nonce k . When a prover generates a commitment R = gk mod p , the security of the private key x depends entirely on the unpredictability of k .

articles.body: Introdução Na parte 1 a gente usou map , takeUntil e switchMap no cronômetro, e pediu para aceitar isso sem olhar por dentro. O problema é que, sem entender o que é um operator, o pipe vira uma caixa preta, e também fica difícil montar uma search-as-you-type sem disparar uma enxurrada de buscas a cada tecla. Neste artigo a gente vai ver o que é um operator, os que usamos no dia a dia, e no final construir esse campo que filtra os resultados conforme a pessoa escreve. Os exemplos usam RxJS 7 (7.8.x). Todos os trechos de código deste artigo foram executados, e as saídas mostradas são as saídas reais. O que é um operator interval e fromEvent são funções de criação, e criam observables do nada. Já map , filter e takeUntil são operators , e recebem um observable e devolvem outro observable.

articles.body: Disclosure: AI assistance was used in preparing this article. The code is an illustrative research example, not a production risk engine or investment recommendation. A portfolio can appear diversified under normal market conditions and still become highly exposed when several risk factors deteriorate together. For example, a digital-asset portfolio may face: Falling BTC and ETH prices. Rising implied volatility. Higher cross-asset correlation. Reduced order-book depth. Wider execution spreads. Testing these conditions independently may miss the combined effect. A more useful approach is to define coherent scenarios, apply their shocks to portfolio positions, and separately account for stressed execution costs. 1.

articles.title: How to politely quit every open app on macOS, Linux and Windows (and the bug my tests missed) published: false
articles.excerpt: At the end of most days I have 15+ apps open. I wanted one command that closes them all, except the terminal I'm typing in, without losing unsaved work. killall and taskkill /f are out: they kill proc…
articles.body: At the end of most days I have 15+ apps open. I wanted one command that closes them all, except the terminal I'm typing in, without losing unsaved work. killall and taskkill /f are out: they kill processes, and unsaved documents die with them. What I wanted was the same thing as pressing Cmd+Q or clicking the X on every app: a polite request the app can answer with "Save changes?". So I built lightsout , a small Go CLI. This post covers how "quit politely" works on each OS, and the bug that taught me to stop trusting green tests. The rules Only close apps a person would see as "open": Dock apps, taskbar apps, windows on screen. No background daemons. Never force-kill. Send the normal close request, wait up to 10 seconds, and report anything still open instead of killing it.

articles.title: Our AI assistant can write to exactly one table. Postgres enforces it, not our code
articles.excerpt: We build Reperline, a small system that tracks construction schedules, budgets and contracts. It also connects to Claude through MCP (Model Context Protocol), so a project manager can ask "which miles…
articles.body: We build Reperline , a small system that tracks construction schedules, budgets and contracts. It also connects to Claude through MCP (Model Context Protocol), so a project manager can ask "which milestones are late?" or upload an invoice and have Claude prepare the entry. That second part is where it gets uncomfortable. Budget data is money. We did not want "the AI only proposes changes" to be a promise made by application code that one refactor could break. We wanted the database to make it impossible. This post is how we set that up in Postgres, and the one default that quietly undid part of it. Two database roles, two very different grants The web app and the MCP server connect as different Postgres roles. Neither has BYPASSRLS . app_rw is the web app.

articles.body: I spent an afternoon pushing one photo through a compression pipeline at every setting it has. These are file sizes from a single source image on a single machine — no benchmarks, just bytes, because "quality 80" tells you nothing until you know what it does to the file. Source: one 6,016 x 6,016 JPEG, 4.80 MB, already encoded around quality 80. Output File size quality 30 0.62 MB quality 60 1.88 MB quality 80 4.80 MB quality 90 5.46 MB quality 100 12.09 MB resized to 1200px wide 0.07 MB same image saved as PNG 30.57 MB 1. Above ~85, quality is a size knob, not a sharpness knob Quality 90 cost 14% more bytes than 80. Quality 100 cost 152% more — 12.09 MB for one image. You will not see that difference at 100% zoom on a laptop screen.

articles.body: SpaceX plans to catch the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), and you can watch the action live. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen, however; SpaceX diverted Starship's Super Heavy booster to a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that remain unclear. But a catch of the Ship upper stage is still on the table, and that would be historic in itself: SpaceX has never tried it before.

articles.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
articles.excerpt: The red planet Mars will shine a little over 1 degree from Jupiter on the night of Nov. 15-16.
articles.body: Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth .

articles.body: Warning! Spoilers for The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Episodes 1-4 follow. If you’re caught up with The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power , you’ll have watched Season 3, Episode 4 and were probably left reeling by a shock character death that leaves the elves in a spot of bother going into the final stretch. During the first four episodes of Season 3, we see Theo, played by Tyroe Muhafidin, tempted by Sauron into becoming a Nazgnagôl. Nazgnagôl are men who wear one of Sauron’s Rings of Power, but still retain something of their humanity. That is, they are not fully Nazgûl, or Ringwraiths, as we know of the beings in the Third Age of J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth. They are, at this stage, Ring Servants.

articles.excerpt: SpaceX's Starship megarocket reached orbit today (Nov. 13) during its 15th test flight, but the company scrapped a plan to catch the vehicle's massive booster back at the launch site.
articles.body: STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona.
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

articles.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?

articles.body: This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed.

articles.title: 100 launches! Rocket Lab sends Earth-observing satellite to orbit on milestone mission (photos)
articles.excerpt: Rocket Lab launched its 100th space mission shortly after midnight on Saturday (Nov. 14), sending a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite to orbit.
articles.body: Rocket Lab just hit the century mark. An Electron rocket topped with a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite lifted off from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site on Saturday (Nov. 14) at 12:30 a.m. EST (0530 GMT; 6:30 p.m. local New Zealand time). The mission, which Rocket Lab called "The Mountain God Rises," was a big one: It marked the 100th launch to date for the California-based company. The first stage of Rocket Lab's Electron rocket falls back to Earth during "The Mountain God Rises" mission on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) Rocket Lab launched for the first time in May 2017, sending the brand-new Electron up on a test flight from New Zealand.

articles.title: 'Arrival' at 10: Denis Villeneuve's alien visitation classic that reminded us it's good to talk
articles.excerpt: How the 'Dune' director turned a little-known short story into one of the best sci-fi movies of the 21st century
articles.body: In many of the biggest science fiction franchises, conversing with alien races is an absolute doddle. In " Star Trek ", universal translators come as standard, while C-3PO has spent the last 49 years reminding everyone in "Star Wars" that he's fluent in over six million forms of communication. But in "Arrival" — which was released 10 years ago in November 2016 — making first contact proves to be rather more challenging than maintaining your Duolingo streak. In fact, working out how to establish a dialogue with extraterrestrial visitors becomes the whole point of this powerful and heartbreaking story, as the fate of planet Earth hinges on the interpretation of a single noun.

articles.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
articles.excerpt: "SignDrop" exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.
articles.body: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System. Turning a Windows defense against itself The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions.
